title: Number Day
strapline: Numbers everywhere — count them, spot them, wear them, play them.
intent: A whole day given to numbers makes maths playful, joyful and everywhere, building a love of number from the start.
Counting, spotting and matching numbers all day deepens number sense, one-to-one counting and recognition.
Number games and challenges weave in subitising, comparing, adding and pattern in a hands-on way.
Finding numbers in the real world — on doors, clocks, phones, dice — shows children maths is all around them.
The day celebrates that everyone can be a mathematician, having a go and enjoying number.
implementation: Fill the day with number play — counting collections, number hunts, dice and dominoes, number songs and rhymes.
Invite children to wear or make a number, and spot numbers around the room and outdoors.
Weave in real counting all day — snack, register, steps, how many children at the water tray.
Offer challenges at every level — matching numerals to amounts, subitising dots, comparing which has more.
Sing number rhymes and act them out — five little ducks, ten in the bed — so number lives in song.
Follow the children — some will count everything in sight, others will play number games for hours.
key_questions: How many can you count — shall we check together?
Can you find a number three anywhere in the room?
Which pile has more — how do you know?
How many dots without counting — can you just see it?

impact.text: Children count collections accurately with one-to-one correspondence.
Children subitise small amounts and compare which has more.
Children recognise and match numerals in the world around them.
Children join in number songs and rhymes and act them out.
Children use maths in play naturally and solve real number problems.

enhancements: A number hunt around the room and garden — spot and photograph numbers in the real world.
A counting-collections table — buttons, conkers, pom-poms — with numeral cards to match.
Dice, dominoes and number games for subitising and comparing.
Number-song props — five ducks, ten in the bed — for singing and acting.
A wear-a-number or make-a-number craft station.

playing_exploring: Children count, sort and play with numbers everywhere, for the joy of it.
They hunt for numbers in the real world with curiosity.
active_learning: Children stick with counting challenges and number games.
They keep going until a collection is counted or a puzzle solved.
creating_thinking: Children reason about amounts — more, fewer, the same.
They spot patterns and predict what number comes next.
